Thanks for the context. Short answer: we need the paper trail to support whichever entity is invoicing. Two practical options and the tax/legal implications: 

1) If Arauz Technologies, Inc. (DE) will invoice and you will pay that entity: we need a completed W-9, plus one of the following to validate the EIN: an IRS TIN-match confirmation (preferred), a bank letter on bank letterhead showing the EIN, or a copy of the Delaware formation + IRS CP575 (EIN issuance letter). If we pay a US entity there should be no US withholding, but we must ensure the contracting party on the SOW aligns with the invoicing party (or a clear subcontracting clause).

2) If Arauz Group S.A. de C.V. (MX) is the contracting party and will invoice: we need a completed W-8BEN-E, a Mexican tax residency certificate if they claim treaty benefits, and the Beneficial Owner Declaration. In that case, we may need to apply 30% withholding unless they claim treaty relief and provide valid documentation.

Recommendation: ask the vendor to confirm which legal entity will be paid, provide the matching tax form, and attach a short explanation of the corporate payment flow (who issues invoices, who signs contracts).

Operational suggestion: Procurement can issue a conditional PO with a note: "Conditional release pending EIN verification / tax form validation — see PROC-2147." That will allow the vendor to proceed with onboarding while payment is staged. Marissa — if Treasury agrees, we'll set a 30-day hold and request documentation by the PO payment milestone.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
